gen-gf-snowburst-one-general-sans: Snowburst One cuts its letters like a stencil sheet, with wide bridges between them and tall lowercase that stands up loud. General Sans follows with smooth, unbroken curves and a steady pen pressure.
gen-luckiest-guy-poppins: Poppins rolls along in rope-loose curves with no flicker between heavy and light, and its lowercase stands tall and sturdy. Luckiest Guy brings the cheerful shout, ink poured at a single width.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-fs-chillax: Chillax reads loose and relaxed, its spaghetti line lifting off the paper before each loop quite closes. Happy Monkey stays ruler-straight up top, so extended reading feels easygoing and unhurried.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-fs-plein: Straight-ruled, bold and distinctive, with wide gaps in every e. Plein tucks a clear channel into each round letter, giving Happy Monkey's unstressed curves a dependable partner beside them.
gen-gf-revalia-switzer: Wide-striding, bold letters, with a g whose lower curve stays open. Revalia keeps that loose stride, while Switzer's wire-like, constant-width line makes extended reading feel approachable and pleasantly tidy.
gen-gf-warnes-general-sans: Ink strokes taper out before they touch, and Warnes spreads them wide with no stroke contrast at all. General Sans fills each line with smooth strokes and steady pen pressure.
gen-irish-grover-work-sans: Work Sans keeps things contemporary, with c tips that never creep together. Irish Grover's tall, sturdy lowercase and open-throated letters give a warm, organic start, so long reading stays easygoing.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-manrope: A splayed c terminal marks Tilt Neon, whose tube-like, constant-width strokes feel bold and commanding at any size. Manrope's open-mouthed curves and minimal capital step keep things approachable below.
gen-gf-unica-one-montserrat: Wire-smooth lines glide under the eye, with generous white space leading into every curve. Montserrat owns that ease, while Unica One's commanding, single-thickness strokes do the shouting up top.
gen-gf-wallpoet-montserrat: Wallpoet lets the paper show through between its bold, commanding letters, while its lowercase rises high and proud. Montserrat does the gliding, with wire-like ease and a constant stroke weight.
